title: Impact of Charging Patterns on Electric Vehicle Battery Lifespan Under Realistic Transient Operation: An Electrochemical Modeling Study
abstract: ABSTRACT Electric vehicles' (EVs) battery lifespan is highly influenced by factors such as temperature, charge/discharge rates (C‐rates), depth‐of‐discharge (DoD), and state‐of‐charge (SoC). While many studies explore these factors under controlled laboratory conditions, this study examines their effects on degradation in realistic transient operating scenarios. Based on a physics‐based simulation methodology that couples an electrochemical model with a lumped thermal model, a 58 Ah pouch cell is parameterized, calibrated, and validated against experimental results. The model accounts for SEI formation and lithium plating, predicting battery degradation. The battery pack powers a 70 kWh EV, which follows a repetitive weekly pattern of driving, charging, and rest. WLTC driving and annual temperature distributions are considered. Firstly, demonstrations show that, at the beginning of life (BoL), starting from 80% SoC and 20°C, the actual driving charge/discharge pattern could induce a higher loss of lithium inventory compared to constant current charge/discharge at the equivalent average C‐rate for the test case studied here. The results show that as the charge rate increases, DoD has a more dominant impact on longevity than mean SoC. Strategically managing DoD and SoC can offset the impact of fast charging. Moreover, charging directly before operation, thereby limiting high SoC storage, extends lifetime up to 13.8%, with relative improvements being more pronounced at intermediate SoC windows and peaking at the 30%–70% SoC range. When temperature is effectively regulated, higher mean SoCs remain the primary aging factor. The paper highlights the value of model‐assisted battery aging studies towards understanding relevant degradation mechanisms and accordingly optimizing charging patterns.

title: Justice-Weighted Vehicle-to-Grid Energy Communities with Calibrated Battery Costs, Network Envelopes, and On-Demand Blockchain Verification
abstract: Peer-to-peer electricity trading with vehicle-to-grid (V2G) support is often proposed for EU energy communities, yet battery wear, network limits, fairness, and the blockchain’s role are usually treated separately. An end-to-end framework is demonstrated on a metered campus community in Cluj-Napoca, Romania, and a reparametrized Budapest (Hungary) twin over 2025. A Bayesian aging model calibrated on field and laboratory data gives each vehicle a temperature and state-of-charge-dependent V2G cost and bid at its 80th percentile. A rolling-horizon market respects network operating envelopes and owners’ mobility. A justice-weighted settlement adds priority matching of vulnerable members, an individual-rationality guarantee, and a solidarity share. Smart contracts commit daily Merkle roots, verify settlements on demand, and enforce the justice rule monthly. The market lowers community costs by 9.6–9.7%, and V2G owners obtain a net margin over expected wear of €826–949 per vehicle per year. At the parity point, the vulnerable members’ share of the gain rises from 5–20% to 38–45% at no efficiency cost, with no member worse off. As deliberate bounding findings, on-chain clearing would need 191 times more gas, and Romania–Hungary trading adds at most 0.3% of costs, even with tripled local PV. Rankings hold for 2023 prices and weather and ±30% driving.

title: Integrating Energy-Efficient Light Sources and Sensors with Room-Temperature Quantum Devices: Applications in Medical Diagnostics, Battery Monitoring, and Quantum Communications / 省エネ光源・センサ技術と常温量子デバイスの統合:医療計測・バッテリー診断・通信分野への応用展望
abstract: [Abstract / English]This paper presents a comprehensive technical framework for integrating energy-efficient, low-heat solid-state light sources (such as LEDs) and optical sensors with cryogen-free, room-temperature quantum devices, typified by diamond nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers and solid-state color centers. Eliminating bulky cryogenic cooling infrastructure while pairing solid-state quantum platforms with compact, ultra-low-power LED excitation and optical readout systems unlocks scalable field deployment across three critical domains:(1) Medical & Biomedical Diagnostics: Non-invasive biomagnetic sensing (magnetocardiography/magnetoencephalography), cellular-scale nanoscale thermometry, and point-of-care immunoassay diagnostics without magnetically shielded rooms or liquid helium;(2) Battery & Power Infrastructure Monitoring: High-precision, non-destructive internal current distribution imaging, micro-short detection, and State-of-Health (SoH) / State-of-Charge (SoC) diagnostics for EVs and autonomous energy storage grids; and(3) Quantum & Optical Communications: Electrically driven room-temperature single-photon LEDs and low-power optical-quantum transceivers enabling edge-deployable Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) and tamper-evident physical infrastructure links.System architectures, power-thermal trade-offs, and engineering roadmaps toward autonomous physical infrastructure integration are systematically examined. [要旨 / 日本語]本稿では、LEDをはじめとする省電力・低発熱な固体光源および光学センサ技術と、ダイヤモンドNVセンター等の固体欠陥に代表される常温動作量子デバイスを統合した次世代システムアーキテクチャと応用展望を論じる。大型かつ高消費電力な極低温冷却設備を排し、常温量子プラットフォームに小型・高効率なLED励起系および光学読み出し系を統合することで、以下の主要3領域における社会実装と自律分散展開が可能となる。(1)医療・生体計測分野:液体ヘリウムや大型磁気シールドルームを必要としない非侵襲生体磁気計測(心磁図・脳磁図等)、低発熱性を活かした細胞レベルのナノ温度計測、および超高感度な医療診断(POCT)センサへの展開。(2)バッテリー診断・電力インフラ分野:EV(電気自動車)や定置型蓄電池における充放電時の微小磁場・内部電流分布の非破壊リアルタイム可視化、微小短絡・劣化兆候の早期検知、ならびに高精度な残量・健全性(SoC/SoH)診断。(3)通信・セキュリティ分野:常温電流注入型単一光子LEDおよび省電力光量子トランシーバによる、エッジ端末・自律物理インフラ網向けの省エネ量子暗号通信(QKD)および高信頼光通信基盤の構築。本論文では、これら3領域における基本構成、省電力・熱設計上の優位性、および実用化に向けた工学的課題を体系的に整理する。 ========================================================================Sovereign Open-Read & Strict No-Learn License (NLL-v1.0-2026) Copyright © 2026 Yoko Hasebe. title: Data-driven intelligent predictive networks for lithium-ion battery state of charge estimation
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries have the characteristics of efficient charging, large specific energy, and long cycle. The battery state of charge (SOC) is an important parameter for battery management systems and is defined as the ratio of the remaining capacity of the battery to its nominal capacity. The direct and accurate prediction of SOC is difficult due to the nonlinear dynamic characteristics and complex charging/discharging cycles. This study presents data-driven nonlinear autoregressive exogenous neuroarchitecture optimized with Levenberg–Marquardt (NARX-NA-LM) and Bayesian regularization (NARX-NA-BR) algorithms for accurate and robust SOC estimation. The performance of the proposed NARX-NA-LM and NARX-NA-BR is investigated in detail for five temperature conditions ([Formula: see text]C, [Formula: see text]C, [Formula: see text]C, [Formula: see text]C, [Formula: see text]C) under four operating conditions. The four operating conditions are based on the data from the highway fuel economy driving schedule, urban dynamometer driving schedule profile, US06 supplemental federal test procedure, and the Los Angeles 92 profile. Accurate SOC prediction supports the proposed scheme, while the MSE-based learning plots for training/testing, error histogram results, correlation statistics, and state transition outcomes verify its convergence and reliability. Generally, the NARX-NA-LM provides better SOC prediction results than the NARX-NA-BR. The NARX-NA-LM is examined in detail for both open-loop and closed-loop configurations, as well as random and sequential data partitioning strategies. The proposed NARX-NA-LM network demonstrated high SOC prediction accuracy across four driving cycles and five operating temperatures ([Formula: see text]C to [Formula: see text]C), with results averaged over 10 independent runs yielding mean absolute errors (MAEs) ranging from 0.00052% to 0.00078% and root mean square errors (RMSEs) ranging from 0.00080% to 0.00181% across the investigated conditions.
